newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Hang Seng Index scores another record close.
newsitem.headline: HK's Hang Seng Index scores another record close.

text.p: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index scored another all-time closing high on Thursday, as investors snatched up stocks which were left behind in Wednesday's record-breaking rally.

The Hang Seng index soared above the 14,000 point-level for the first time this session, hitting a record high of 14,004.93 before closing on a gain of 64.03 points at 13,830.68. Turnover was a massive HK$16.23 billion, the third largest ever.
"I think there are a lot of momentum players around and a lot of people were caught short of the sharp break-out yesterday," said James Osborn, sales director at ING Barings.
"There is a bit of laggard buying," he added.
The Hang Seng posted its third-biggest point gain ever on Wednesday, climbing 472.78 points as property and banking stocks surged. Utilities and conglomerates played catch up on Thursday.
Wheelock rose HK$1.10 to HK$22.40 and CITIC Pacific gained HK$1.10 to HK$41.70. In the utilities sector, China Light gained HK$0.30 to HK$34.20 and Hongkong Telecom HK$0.25 to HK$13.35.
"I think it is just rotational buying," said Gilbert Chu, head of research at SocGen-Crosby Securities.
Analysts said the index had met with resistance after venturing above 14,000 points on Thursday.
"There is bound to be a bit of psychological stuttering at 14,000 but technically it should be irrelevant," said Osborn. He saw tougher resistance at 14,200 points.

"I think the market is overbought but it does seem to be continuing for the moment and it is hard to say when it is going to turn," said Chu. "The market breaking out of its previous highs is attracting buying interest from locals and foreigners. We have seen a lot of derivatives being issued which has been driving the market. It is creating a lot of liquidity," he said.
Osborn said recent issues of covered warrants had created demand for HK$4 billion to HK$5 billion worth of stock.

"I think people feel that from a value point of view the market is in no man's land. It is not going to go up and it is not going to go down. No one is really going to sell into this rise at the moment," Osborn added.
Shares of HSBC traded at a record high of HK$183.00 on Thursday before closing on a gain of HK$2.00 at HK$181.00.
Great Eagle Holdings rose HK$1.10 to HK$35.10 after posting a 28.7 percent rise in net profit for the year ended September 30, 1996 to HK$1.06 billion.
Cheung Kong fell HK$1.75 to HK$76.00 and Henderson Land slipped HK$0.25 to HK$75.50.
